flags.reason: Two managed chronic conditions with a 0-month stated horizon against Balanced's 6-month chronic wait. Cover is real but not immediate — confirm the applicant understands the first six months.

recommendation.brokerReasoning: Genuinely arguable between Balanced and Comprehensive — the closest call of the five. Both cover chronic pre-existing; they differ on when (6 months vs 0) and on price (8,900 vs 16,500). Conditions are managed and stable on medication, so the first six months carry routine follow-up cost, not clinical risk. Stated priorities name cost explicitly alongside chronic depth. Balanced wins on 7,600 of annual saving against a bounded six-month gap. Worth a reviewer's eyes: if the applicant cannot self-fund that window, this flips.
recommendation.memberReasoning: Balanced gives you ongoing cover for your diabetes and blood pressure at 8,900 a year. One thing to plan around: cover for conditions you already have starts after 6 months on the policy, so treatment for those two before then is yours to pay. After that you are covered, with a 500 deductible and 20% of outpatient bills. We chose it over the top plan because that one would cost nearly double and the only real difference for you is those first six months.

rejections.reason: Chronic pre-existing not covered at all — excluded on the applicant's primary need.
Removes the 6-month chronic wait, which is the only material difference here, at 7,600 a year more. On stable managed conditions that is a poor trade against a stated cost priority.
